msg: DESIGN TARGET (blocks.md B4). THE SHIPPING CIRCUIT: no isolation resistor, CL = 1 nF (REQUIREMENTS Q8 worst case), calibrated ro = 1 kohm, whole signal path. Measured 0.61 % overshoot at J2. This is the claim the board now rests on after R6 was removed at P4.
DESIGN TARGET. Control: with no cable (CL = 1 pF) there must be no overshoot at all. Measured 0.0 %.
Same control on the pessimistic ro = 2 kohm bracket. Measured 0.0 %.

REQUIREMENTS Q8 (load > 100 kohm) + blocks.md B5, which rejected any series output resistor because it 'would add a divider error into a 100 k load'. With no isolation resistor the delivered span is 99.97 % of the unloaded 2.7848 V design span, which is that objection answered. MUTATION-VERIFIED: a 10 k series element reads 90.9 %.
DESIGN TARGET, shipping circuit on the pessimistic ro = 2 kohm bracket. Measured 2.91 %.

EVIDENCE GUARD, not a board bound (which is why it is a warning): overshoot at riso = 0 minus overshoot at riso = 1 k, calibrated ro, measured +0.15 points. It guards the ungated riso sweep that documents WHY R6 was removed - if the sign ever inverts, the removal argument has to be re-derived rather than re-run.
Same evidence guard on the pessimistic bracket: +1.00 points.
EVIDENCE, kept from the R6 comparison: the 100 R that was fitted at P3 delivered 99.87 % of span. Recorded so the cost side of the removal stays reproducible.
EVIDENCE, kept from the R6 comparison: with 100 R fitted the full path overshot 0.63 %, i.e. 0.02 points WORSE than with none. On the real signal path R6 = 100 R did nothing.

EVIDENCE, kept from the R6 comparison: riso = 1 kohm - the value that would actually isolate - reaches 0.47 %, at 1.0 % of span (sp_a_r1k) and a -5 %-rail full scale of about 2.994 V, below blocks.md B6.
